newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Caldera signs Labor Reform into law.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Caldera signs Labor Reform into law.

text.p: President Rafael Caldera signed into law Thursday Venezuela's milestone Labor Law Reform bill which paves the way for a complete overhaul of the country's decaying social security system.
"I can't hide the satisfaction that this gives me," Caldera said during the ceremonial signing that was broadcast live nationwide on both television and radio.
The bill tackles the complex and controversial reform of Venezuela's onerous and outdated severance/pension payment system.

Although its implementation will cost some $8 billion spread over five years, many analysts view the reform as the most significant of Caldera's administration as it paves the way for more flexible labor markets and hence greater productivity.
"The immense sacrifice that the Venezuelan state has made for its workers ... is greater than any other state of any other country ... we believe in social justice," a tremulous Caldera said.
With the signing, a new urban minimum wage of 75,000 bolivars per month also comes into effect, 44 percent higher than the previous minimum legal take-home pay of 52,000 bolivars.
